The boundary factor is the difference between the native and the common-boundary gap.

clocks.ic_A: koblitz_orbit_dlp_fast: target_ms from query_started (before the scan-origin hash) to after the [d]G = Q recovery check; five laps target_query/pdp/relation_check/descent/recovery_check with a sub-microsecond residual
clocks.ic_B: koblitz_orbit_dlp_fast_online(+patch): online_ms from target_query_begin (the same scan-origin hash) to recovery_check_end; the same five laps on one PhaseClock, summing exactly; base, normal basis, root index and (cached) table load + full [L_j]G = R_j verification or (fresh) rank stage + linear algebra are excluded

Curve, normal basis and 32 G-only jumps are excluded (preparation_ns_excluded).

Curve, normal basis, the 32 G-only jumps and the public-point membership/subgroup check (target_generation_ms_excluded) are excluded.

controls.aa_ic: iB770caa - iB770c per block; same pass rule; probes must be identical
controls.aa_rho: rA770aa - rA770, mean over the six seeds, per block; pass if the 95% interval of its block mean lies in [-0.05, 0.05] and |mean| <= 0.03; walk steps must be identical
identity_checks: every arm on a point recovers the same scalar; Q0's equals fixture_scalar_validation_only; each point's scalar replays as [d]G = Q in oracle.py
rA819, rA770 and rA770aa take identical walk steps per seed (StrongRhoG's walk is unchanged between the revisions); each rho arm's steps per (seed, point) are identical across blocks
every IC arm on a point takes identical probes (expected 8,845,441 on Q0) and every fresh rank arm reaches rank 600
every iB770f table's 600 logs equal B's archived table's logs
controls.positive_control: known effect from an exact computation: ln(rA770 time at seed 202610064 / at seed 202610063) must be within 0.10 of ln(walk steps 202610064 / walk steps 202610063) (A's receipts: 14,229,982 / 5,353,957, ln = 0.978); shows the timing instrument resolves an effect of the size under study

decision_rule.contention: isolated_bench's Tier 1 noise gate (cgroup nr_throttled/throttled_usec, steal on the execution CPU, major faults) is recorded per row as contention_flags. Flagged rows stay in the analysis; the decision is recomputed on the Q blocks with no flagged row, and if it names a different responsible set (or fewer than 3 such blocks remain) the reading is sensitive_to_contention. Fresh-rank IC arms run about 15 min, so a steal tick during their excluded setup is plausible; that is why flags do not void a row.
decision_rule.controls: inconclusive_controls if either A/A control or the positive control fails; the factor table is still reported, labelled as such

factor_classes.contributes: Bonferroni 99.29% interval of D_f excludes 0 and |mean D_f| >= 0.05
factor_classes.sufficient_to_flip: A_reproduces and L_A + D_f has a Bonferroni 99.29% lower bound > 0 (applying f alone to A's configuration makes IC online faster)

reproduction.A_reproduces: L_A 95% upper bound < 0 (rho online faster with A's configuration on the runner)

decision_rule.responsible: If A_not_reproduced: 'host_or_instance' (A's direction does not survive the move to this runner) is named responsible, and the chain factors are reported as modifiers. Else, if A_reproduces and B_reproduces: every sufficient_to_flip factor is named, ranked by mean D_f; if none is sufficient alone, the smallest set of contributing factors, taken in decreasing order of mean D_f, whose summed per-block effect makes L_A + sum have a Bonferroni lower bound > 0. If B does not reproduce, B's Q0 direction is reported as instance-specific and the responsible set is 'host_or_instance' for B. Otherwise not_separated.
decision_rule.validity: no_result unless every executed row of the counted segments is valid (exit 0, verified=1, no timeout, no cgroup memory event oom/oom_kill/max, binary unchanged), every identity check passes, and at least 3 Q blocks and 12 fresh points completed. Invalid rows are kept and reported; no row is re-run.
decision_rule.what_does_not_count: changing blocks, seeds, points, arms, statistics or thresholds after seeing any timing; any such change is a new, labelled protocol version reported beside this one. The verdict is about one target (Q0) and one runner for the chain, and 16 points for the rho factors over targets; it is not a speed claim for either method.

design.envelope: one process at a time on one pinned exposed CPU (the lowest CPU of the runner's affinity mask), sched_setaffinity before exec, RAYON/KIC thread variables 1, clean whitelisted environment, no builds or other heavy jobs during the panel
design.minimum_for_a_result: 3 complete Q blocks and 12 complete fresh points
design.order: segments Q1, F(points 0-3), Q2, F(4-7), Q3, F(8-11), Q4, F(12-15); inside a Q block the 35 runs are in a frozen pseudo-random order (random.Random(2026101400 + block).shuffle); inside an F segment the points run in order and each point's 9 runs are shuffled with random.Random(2026101500 + w). make_schedule.py writes schedule.json from this protocol; the workflow regenerates it and requires byte identity.
design.time_guard: before each segment, if (now - job start) + max(the segment's frozen upper estimate, 1.1 x the longest segment of the same panel already run in this job) exceeds 325 min, the segment and all later ones are recorded as skipped_time_guard and not run; a skipped segment is never re-run or replaced
design.type: full factorial in analysis, by complete blocks: every arm runs in every Q0 block, so every rho-arm x seed x IC-arm combination is a within-block paired ratio. Crossed factors: rho implementation (3 levels: A default, B rung 3, A tuned) x rho seed set (SA, SB) on Q0 and (SA_rule, SB_rule) on fresh points. Nested where the code does not exist: rho revision only for A's default rho (rung 3 has no n=83 wide path at a8194d61); IC revision only for A's producer; IC log source only for B's producer (A's producer has no cache). The IC chain A -> B is therefore revision (iA819f -> iA770f), producer (iA770f -> iB770f), log source (iB770f -> iB770c).

frozen_files_note: checked by verify_receipt.py against the files at audit time; schedule.json is also regenerated and compared by the workflow

question: Why do two measurements of the same n=83 a=1 point Q0 disagree in direction? A (crypto research/n83_evaluation_20261012, 2026-10-12): IC/strong-rho online 1.38 [1.04, 1.88] (rho faster). B (cryptanalysis experiments/koblitz-single-target-n83-tier1-20261014, run 38523707244): rho/IC online 1.78 [1.775, 1.783] on Q0 (IC faster). Identify which factor(s) flip the direction by re-running both configurations and every intermediate one, interleaved, in one job on one GitHub ubuntu-24.04 runner, on the same points.

estimate_s.basis: B's runner receipts (run 38523707244): fresh-rank B producer 888 s process wall, cached IC 46.5 s setup + 5.07 s online on Q0, rung 3 0.705 us/step; A's host: A's IC 1,054 s per process; builds here: 5.6 + 4.7 min at -j3

both orders of the implementation x seed chain (interaction = their difference)
the deterministic split of every rho time into ln(steps) + ln(ns per step) and of every IC time into ln(probes) + ln(ns per probe)

chain.boundary: ln rB770[SB] at B's boundary - the same run at A's boundary (IC boundaries are identical by audit; their phase sums are checked per row)
chain.identity: rev_rho + impl_rho + seed + boundary + rev_ic + prod_ic + cache = G exactly, per block
chain.impl_rho: Shapley value over {implementation, seed}: half of [(mean_SA ln rB770 - mean_SA ln rA770) + (ln rB770[SB] - ln rA770[SB])], rB770 at the A boundary
chain.rev_rho: mean_SA ln rA770 - mean_SA ln rA819 (A boundary)
chain.seed: Shapley value: half of [(ln rA770[SB] - mean_SA ln rA770) + (ln rB770[SB] - mean_SA ln rB770)], rB770 at the A boundary

contrasts.seed_family_negative_control: mean over the four rho arms of ln rho(830000 + w) - ln rho(202610061 + w); expected 0, it is a seed relabeling

f_panel.interval: 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the 16 points (seed 2026101402), percentile 95%
f_panel.per_point: x[w, arm] = mean over the two seeds of ln rho; y[w] = ln iB770c
f_panel.section_23_per_rho_arm: mean over points of rho online / mean over points of IC online (B's Panel B statistic), and the median of per-point ratios

statistics.q_interval: per-block values; 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the blocks (seed 2026101401); percentile 95% interval, and the Bonferroni 99.29% interval (m = 7 chain factors) for the factor classification. With 4 blocks these intervals cover repeat/timing variation on one target, not seed or target variation: the seed sets are fixed and their effect is conditional on them.

q_panel_cells.L_A: A's configuration on the runner, per block: mean over SA of ln rA819 - ln iA819f (A's estimator: geometric mean of per-seed ratios)
q_panel_cells.L_B: B's configuration on the runner, per block: ln rB770[831000] - ln iB770c

statistics.unit: natural log of online ms per run; a ratio R is rho_online_ms / ic_online_ms, so ln R > 0 means IC online is faster
